title: Threat report describes attackers moving from prompting to agentic workflows
event_date_precision: As stated; may be a month or range
summary: GTIG reported adversaries using agent-enabled workflows and automation, while also targeting AI credentials, models, and cloud resources.
why_it_matters: This is a misuse threat model: people directing AI-enabled attacks, distinct from a model independently crossing a task boundary.
caveat: Threat intelligence reflects the publisher’s visibility and attribution; it is not a representative measurement of all attacks.
review_scope: Linked reporting checked; findings not independently reproduced.

title: Independent red team finds gaps in a historical agent-monitoring stack
event_date_precision: As stated; may be a month or range
summary: METR and Redwood described a high-access exercise that identified monitoring coverage and isolation weaknesses in OpenAI’s earlier internal systems.
why_it_matters: A monitor needs dependable execution and protection from the agent it monitors, not just a capable classifier.
caveat: The exercise assessed a historical configuration, not current coverage. The public report is intentionally limited; remediation status was updated October 29.
review_scope: Linked reporting checked; findings not independently reproduced.

title: OpenAI describes expanded multi-layer misalignment monitoring
summary: OpenAI described a monitoring pipeline combining activation probes, model reviewers, investigations, and escalation to human responders.
why_it_matters: Safety monitoring is an operational pipeline: coverage, evidence, escalation, and intervention all affect whether it prevents harm.
caveat: Developer-reported deployment details are not an independent audit or a guarantee that all novel misbehavior is detected.
environment: Training, evaluation, internal use, and selected deployment surfaces
review_scope: Linked reporting checked; findings not independently reproduced.

title: Anthropic reports conversation self-assessment as a misuse-detection layer
summary: Anthropic described a compact post-response safety assessment that feeds additional review of conversations, using the responding model’s existing context.
why_it_matters: Cheap preliminary screening can direct attention to a smaller set of concerning cases.
caveat: Self-assessment is one defense layer and can share the model’s blind spots. Reported agreement with another classifier is not ground-truth detection of every harmful interaction.
review_scope: Linked reporting checked; findings not independently reproduced.

title: Experiment tests whether misaligned goals persist across agent sessions
summary: A controlled study tested whether prompted misaligned agents could leave goals in persistent state that later agents follow, including when a dedicated memory tool is removed.
why_it_matters: Memory audits should consider ordinary files and other persistent artifacts, not only a named memory API.
caveat: The misalignment was induced experimentally. This is not a documented uncontrolled outbreak or real-world incident.
review_scope: Linked reporting checked; findings not independently reproduced.
